selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main image is used at the beginning of the passage to describe the universe?
questions.answer: The universe is pictured as a written book filled with meaning and signs.

questions.question: In that opening image, what does the “pen” represent?
questions.answer: It represents divine power bringing things into being and marking them with meaning.

questions.question: What is being said about the ability of a sincere heart to notice truth in the world?
questions.answer: It is being said that a spiritually awake heart can recognize clear signs of Allah in creation.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the amount of meaning found in the world-book?
questions.answer: It presents that meaning as vast and beyond counting, with endless dimensions and countless events.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about each created thing when it calls every being a meaningful embodied word?
questions.answer: Each being is treated as a meaningful sign that carries a message about reality and its Creator.

questions.question: According to the passage, what shared declaration do all things make together?
questions.answer: They all testify to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Besides affirming divine oneness, what two divine addresses are mentioned as being called out in harmony?
questions.answer: They call upon Allah as the True One and the Living One.

questions.question: What central conclusion is drawn from the claim that every thing contains a sign?
questions.answer: The conclusion is that every created thing points toward the unity of Allah.

questions.question: How do the heart and the nafs respond after hearing this message?
questions.answer: They both accept it and confirm it.

questions.question: What comparison shapes most of the passage’s description of the world?
questions.answer: The world is compared to a text that has been written and can be read for meaning.

questions.question: What does the passage imply by saying there is no hidden dark point for the heart’s sight?
questions.answer: It implies that the signs of Allah are openly present and not truly obscure to spiritual perception.

questions.question: How are time and events presented in the passage?
questions.answer: They are presented like written lines that record countless works.

questions.question: What does the mention of the Preserved Tablet add to the passage’s meaning?
questions.answer: It connects worldly beings to a higher divine order and shows that creation is meaningful, measured, and known.

questions.question: In this passage, is creation presented as random or purposeful? Explain briefly.
questions.answer: It is presented as purposeful, because every being is treated as meaningful and sign-bearing.

questions.question: What kind of unity is expressed when all things speak together with one message?
questions.answer: It is a unity of testimony, where all creation agrees in pointing to Allah.

questions.question: Why is the phrase about every thing having a sign so important here?
questions.answer: It sums up the whole passage by teaching that every created thing can lead a person to recognize divine oneness.

questions.question: What is significant about both the heart and the nafs responding positively at the end?
questions.answer: It shows that both deeper spiritual awareness and the lower self are being brought into acknowledgment of the truth.

questions.question: What is the best short summary of the marked passage?
questions.answer: The passage teaches that the whole universe is a meaningful sign system leading the observer to affirm Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What does the passage ask the reader to do first with the universe?
questions.answer: It asks the reader to look carefully at it as something full of meaning.

questions.question: What does the imagery of writing tell us about created things?
questions.answer: It tells us that created things are deliberate signs, not accidental objects.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the scope of the world’s “pages” and “lines”?
questions.answer: It describes them as limitless in extent and countless in their details.

questions.question: What is the relation between a being and a word in the passage’s imagery?
questions.answer: A being is like a word because it expresses meaning beyond itself.

questions.question: What repeated idea ties the poetic lines and the later statement about all things together?
questions.answer: Both parts stress that creation points in a unified way to Allah.

questions.question: What does the unified call of all things teach about the natural world?
questions.answer: It teaches that the natural world is in harmony in bearing witness to one Creator.
